title: Drive straight with the gyro
summary: Correct the heading all the way so the robot really drives straight.
what: The robot drives 80 cm, constantly correcting its direction with the gyro.
why: Real robots never drive perfectly straight: one wheel is a tiny bit bigger, or slips. The gyro notices the robot pointing off course, and the program steers back. This is another P controller: correction = yaw × 2.
try: Set Realism to Challenging. Run ▶×5 with this program and with a plain move 80 cm block. Compare.
Change the gain 2 to 0.5 and to 6. What happens?
Use DriveStraight and TurnRight together to make an accurate square.
The gyro keeps the robot pointing the way it started. If it starts crooked, it drives crooked. How could you line the robot up the same way every time?
